thread:
nidhi-cs: 🚨 Hey team — CS got a high-priority escalation: multiple customers reporting large p95/p99 latency regressions (2-3x) and a few 502s since ~02:10 UTC. Started right after last night's infra rollout.
samir-eng: which rollout? kernel, driver, fw?
nidhi-cs: kernel patch + CUDA 12.2.1 -> 12.3.0 driver rolled out to us-west2 and eu1 between 01:30-02:05 UTC. Affected customers: acme-ads, beta-embed-svc. They reported embedding and generate endpoints most impacted.
devin-infra: can you paste one minimal repro trace or request id? we need to correlate logs.
nidhi-cs: here's a sample request id: req_0x7a9b2f. Trace shows host-side IO waits and then long GPU scheduling stall.
samir-eng: grabbing node logs now. Quick checks: nvme timeouts, dmesg shows a burst of nvme I/O queue full, and nvidia-smi shows driver timeout on one GPU.
nidhi-cs: paste of relevant logs:
```
[  02:12:47] nvme0: I/O 12345 timeout, discarding command
[  02:12:48] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
[  02:12:50] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=1421, GPU stuck
[  02:12:50] systemd: Task <svc-worker> blocked for 252s
```
maya-oncall: ops-bot, run query: top 5 hosts by avg tail latency in us-west2 01:30-02:30 UTC
ops-bot: query results (short): host-37 (p99=1.8s), host-42 (p99=1.6s, nvme errors), host-55 (p99=1.5s)
devin-infra: looks like correlation between nvme queue spikes and the p99. Did the kernel config change I/O scheduler or cgroup limits?
samir-eng: kernel 6.1.0 -> 6.1.14 rolled with updated BFQ qdisc parameters and changed blk_mq tunables. Possible hostfs interference with GPU KV cache flushes.
eli-ml: ML note — our KV cache workload does frequent small random reads during long-context generation; if hostfs stalls, GPU waits for weights or checkpoints. Also embedding pipelines are I/O heavy for vector stores.
frank-support: customers want ETA and mitigation. Any fast mitigations we can push?
maya-oncall: immediate mitigations we can try:
- route critical customers to dedicated nodes in other regions (eu3, us-east) ✅
- reduce batch size / max_concurrency for embeddings to reduce IOPS ✅
- temporarily pin model-serving instances to older kernel/driver images for a canary fleet ⚠️
- enable aggressive KV prefix cache to hit fewer host reads (short term config)
samir-eng: actionable plan:
1) start routing acme-ads and beta-embed-svc traffic to us-east-dedicated-2 and eu3-dedicated-1 (maya)
2) scale up dedicated pools for embedding workloads by +30% (devin)
3) roll back kernel on 10% of affected hosts to 6.1.12 for fast mitigation and test repro (samir + devin)
4) collect full dmesg + iostat + nvidia-smi logs and open driver bug with vendor if we see Xid repeats (eli)
5) add a temporary autoscaler safety cap to avoid bursting too many concurrent jobs (samir)
nidhi-cs: I'll notify customers with mitigation steps and ask them to switch to fallback routes (we can set a tenant routing override)
ops-bot: runbook note created: RB-2026-032-mit-p95-kernel-io
devin-infra: rolling kernel rollback to 10% of hosts in us-west2 (canary). command used:
```
ansible-playbook rollback-kernel.yml -e "hosts=usw2-canary group=serving" --limit host-37,host-42
```
samir-eng: also doing driver bisect on a repro host. repro steps for infra team:
1) use embedding workload: embed-bench --model text-embedding-ada --batch 64 --concurrency 8 --dataset small
2) run for 10 minutes while monitoring iostat -x 1 and nvidia-smi dmon
3) collect /var/log/dmesg and system journal for the window
eli-ml: temporary model-level mitigation: switch embedding customers to smaller model shard (quantized variant) to reduce GPU memory pressure and flush frequency.
frank-support: sending an interim status email to acme-ads and beta-embed-svc noting routing + active mitigation. asking for confirmation on improved latency.
maya-oncall: update: after routing acme-ads to us-east, p99 dropped from ~1.8s -> ~0.45s for them. marking as partial mitigation.
samir-eng: can we confirm if any hosts show firmware updates? nvme firmware changed on some racks last week; cross-checking.
ops-bot: firmware map shows nvme-fw-3.0 applied to rack-4 on 2026-03-10; no new fw this week.
devin-infra: still seeing one repro host with GPU Xid after rollback — might be a driver/kernel interaction. opening escalation with vendor. assigning samir to lead triage.
samir-eng: assigning tasks: devin (rollback execution + fleet health), eli (repro capture + vendor ticket), maya (customer comms), nidhi (CS follow-up), frank (SLA comms). I'll own the bisect.
nidhi-cs: customers acknowledged routing and report improved tail. I'll keep thread open until vendor response. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
frank-support: logging incident for postmortem and RCA — tag: infra-kernel-io-interaction-2026-03-17
maya-oncall: follow-ups: collect metrics for 24h pre/post, vendor ticket #DRV-12588, schedule postmortem tomorrow 15:00 UTC. closing loop once driver/vendor action decided.
samir-eng: noted. will push a short config change to reduce hostfs writeback frequency to limit I/O spikes as an interim config (will test on canary).
nidhi-cs: great. closing temporary customer triage. will update when vendor responds and when postmortem is scheduled.
